initiative.title: Diagram primitives: cells, tables, byte layouts and images
initiative.summary: One `cells` layout recipe on groups draws touching sequences, tables and byte layouts; cells are ordinary nodes so lines, colors and marks reach them. Image cells build on PR #28.
initiative.next_action: Byron answers the product questions; then start M1 (sequences) after plan-grouping and fold-small land.

sources.location: Byron voice memo, 2026-10-26, relayed by orchestrator session local_5d94cf47
sources.anchor: more primitives to recover what Graphviz DOT does
record shapes and HTML-like labels (TABLE, TD PORT, COLSPAN, IMG)

claims.statement: Draftably should cover what Graphviz DOT draws so it can be a general diagram tool.
Sequences: touching boxes show one thing's parts in order, such as a request with a cache point.
Byte layouts like the PNG and PDF spec figures.
Tables on the canvas, like DOT HTML-like table labels.
Images matter most in the viewer; large screenshots scale badly in static exports. Build on PR #28.
Keep the DSL as small as possible.

themes: composite objects made of touching parts
lines to parts of an object
human_questions: One cells recipe or three named statements?
How deep should byte layouts go?
What is the main job of tables?

shape.appetite: Three PRs for sequences, tables and bytes; image cells after PR #28 M1; viewer editing optional.
shape.problem: Sequences, byte layouts and tables need DOT or hand drawing today; Draftably has only separate boxes.
shape.recommended_shape: A `cells` layout recipe on a group. Members touch and share borders; columns=, span=, unit=, ruler= cover tables and byte layouts. Cells are nodes, so edges, colors, marks and compare work unchanged.
success_moves: Reuse group, node, in= and layout instead of a new statement type.
Put cell geometry in one pure function (src/dsl/cells.ts) shared by compile, CLI and viewer.
Prove routing into a mid-row cell in the first PR, with an outline-attach fallback.
Keep src/engines untouched; the root engine moves a cell group as one block.
Ship sequences before tables and bytes; later PRs only change width rules and drawing.

first_proof.question: Can the compiler and router draw touching cells and end a line on one cell?
first_proof.artifact: inspect --svg of examples/prompt-request.draft, and the same file in the viewer
first_proof.decision_rule: If a line to a mid-row cell crosses other cells or needs a new router mode, attach lines at the group outline over the cell's span.

open_decisions: How should static exports treat large images?
Which primitive ships first after sequences?

milestones.title: Sequences of touching cells
milestones.done_when: inspect --svg shows touching cells and a line ending on the hist cell; viewer matches; compiles under engine=layered; pnpm check passes.
milestones.outcome: A group with `layout g cells` draws one strip of touching cells, and a line ends on one cell.
milestones.proof: Unit cases plus inspect --svg and viewer pictures of examples/prompt-request.draft.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Files without `cells` compile exactly as before.
milestones.rollback: Revert the PR; no file uses `cells` yet.

milestones.title: Tables
milestones.done_when: Schema example has aligned columns and foreign-key lines end on rows; check reports a line to an inner cell.
milestones.outcome: Cell groups wrap into grids with shared column widths, spans and one-column entity tables.
milestones.proof: Schema example picture and a column-width test.

milestones.title: Byte layouts
milestones.done_when: TCP header matches RFC 9293 field for field; PNG chunk shows a variable data field.
milestones.outcome: Cell groups with `unit=` draw byte and bit layouts with rulers and split fields.
milestones.proof: TCP and PNG examples compared with their spec figures.

milestones.title: Image cells
milestones.done_when: Two image cells draw the same in CLI and viewer; exports follow PR #28.
milestones.outcome: An image node can be a cell.
milestones.proof: Image-cell example in CLI and viewer.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Text cells unchanged; image nodes outside cells follow PR #28.
milestones.rollback: Revert; image nodes stay outside cell groups.

milestones.title: Viewer editing of cells
milestones.done_when: Reordering a cell writes one order line and the file reopens the same.
milestones.outcome: Viewer drag reorders cells and the inspector edits span.
milestones.proof: Real pointer browser proof; file round-trip.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Cell groups still move as one block.
